features.name: Extract state-layer checks into scripts/state_layer_check.py
features.description: Move the feature_list.json validation out of the inline heredoc in harness/guards/state-layer-guard.sh into scripts/state_layer_check.py with unchanged behavior, refactor scripts/trace_evaluation.py, and make doc links repo-relative.
acceptance_criteria: state-layer-guard.sh blocks with exit 2 for every failure, including a crashing checker and a missing python3
check order and stderr headers match the old heredoc
no file:///Users/... links remain in AGENTS.md or lecture docs
test_state_layer_guard.sh passes on bash 5 and /bin/bash 3.2, and all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: Added scripts/state_layer_check.py; the guard now calls it and maps any non-zero status to exit 2. Independent review (fresh-context subagent plus codex-kiro) found the guard exited 1 or 127 when the checker crashed or python3 was missing, which does not block; fixed with tests, and a self-referential trace_row test now asserts literal values. test_state_layer_guard.sh 44/44 on bash 5 and /bin/bash 3.2, test_session_clean.sh 8/8, tests/test_trace_evaluation.py 7/7. Converted 9 AGENTS.md and 6 lecture-doc file:/// links to relative paths. Dropped the redundant Write() deny rule in .claude/settings.json because Claude Code only consults Edit(path) rules.

features.name: One place per record: remove duplicated docs and lecture engine copies
features.description: Remove records that duplicate another source: recent-tasks-summary.md, the lecture 13/14/15 engine copies and their tests, and the decisions section of progress-archive.md. Record the one-place rule in AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/*_runner.py are the only copies of the ratchet, graph and team engines, and the lecture docs link to them
no reference to a deleted file remains outside historical evidence text
AGENTS.md has a one-place-per-record table; docs/decisions.md holds superseded decisions
all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: Folded the motivation text into docs/architecture.md section 5 and deleted docs/improvements/recent-tasks-summary.md with its AGENTS.md references. Deleted the lecture 13/14/15 engines and their 28 tests; the runner suites (37 tests) and three shell suites still pass. Moved Archived Decisions to docs/decisions.md. Added docs/harness-creator/README.md marking the lectures frozen. Known coverage gaps after the deletion: the checkpoint save-and-resume path of the graph runner is only covered indirectly, and the goal-template.md parse assertions were not ported (docs/goals/TEMPLATE.md is covered by test_ratchet_loop.sh).

features.name: Run telemetry: read-only collector, comparison report, outside-agent attempt log
features.description: Measure token use, duration, subagents and gate results per run from Claude Code session files without relying on the agent's own estimates, keep detail outside the state layer, and record every outside-agent attempt.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/run_telemetry.py deduplicates usage by (scope, message id), flags conflicting rows, never reports an unavailable metric as 0, and keeps parent and subagent usage separate
scripts/run_report.py prints missing metrics as n/a and compares runs in one table
cmd_run records every outside-agent attempt (including failures, timeouts, skips, interruptions) without changing return codes or candidate order
state layer stays within its 6,000-token budget and all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: Collector, report and 53 tests (tests/test_run_telemetry.py, tests/test_run_report.py); 24 baseline records in docs/telemetry/runs/ from 22 existing sessions, with docs/telemetry/RELIABILITY.md listing each metric as measured, ambiguous or missing. Reviews: a fresh subagent and codex-kiro on the first draft found 12 defects (synthetic rows reported a context size of 0 in 4 sessions, 4 nested workflow subagents never read, crashes on non-hashable ids and NaN durations, committed records carrying agent type and session id verbatim, window boundary rows counted twice); each got a failing test first and a fix. Attempt logging for outside_agent.py got a subagent and codex-kiro review; the SIGTERM path was found by both and fixed. Not done: USD cost (no authoritative source), outcome and retries (no structured record), Codex/Kiro/agy token usage (none usable), and running the fixed benchmark defined in docs/stories/run-telemetry/benchmark.md.
features.verification: bash scripts/harness-verify.sh && python3 -m pytest tests/test_run_telemetry.py tests/test_run_report.py tests/test_outside_agent.py -q

features.name: Fixed telemetry benchmark: five tasks, scripted checks, runner and comparison
features.description: Answer whether a harness change made the next task of the same difficulty faster, cheaper or more reliable, using fixed prompts, frozen fixtures, hidden checks and no model-based scoring.
acceptance_criteria: each of B1-B5 has a frozen prompt, a fixture, and scripted checks that fail on the untouched fixture and pass on a reference solution
compare prints no verdict with fewer than 5 runs per version, and only between runs that share model and suite hash
a run's telemetry counts only that run's outside-agent attempts
all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: scripts/telemetry_benchmark.py, benchmarks/telemetry/ (suite, fixtures, hidden tests, reference solutions; python files stored as *.fixture so mypy and the bash guard skip them), tests/test_telemetry_benchmark.py (38 tests, fake agent, no tokens). One real run of each task on claude-sonnet-5.5 passed. Two defects found by the smoke runs (B2 check rejected a legitimate added test; run telemetry counted the global outside-agent log) and 8 more by a fresh subagent plus codex-kiro (hidden dir exposed via BENCH_DIR, first-pass compared as a point, missing subagents read as 0, harness commit turned -dirty by its own output, missing agent binary crashed the batch, B1 accepted a hard-coded answer, B3 matched negated sentences, B5 only checked that ids survived); each got a failing test first. Not done: the 5-runs-per-version comparison itself (about 50 sessions, run it when a harness change needs measuring), gate results per task (fixture repos have no gates), a second harness version to compare against. B3 scoring is keyword-based and can misjudge unusual phrasing.

features.name: Faster gates and automatic run records: parallel tests, process adherence, feature summaries, review timeout
features.description: Cut the verify time, make every task leave its own telemetry without manual steps, and make outside-agent failures explain themselves.
acceptance_criteria: run-tests.sh runs files in parallel and prints the same lines, order, counts and exit code as the sequential run; a killed test is a failure; a signal stops the queue
every run record carries process_adherence (hook feedback, review attempts by family, subagents by type) with unmeasurable rules marked missing

session-clean attaches a summary to each completed feature, archives old features to keep the state layer under 6000 tokens without losing any, and keeps the last gate report for the window it falls in
outside-agent reviews default to 300 s and failed attempts log a bounded, scrubbed reason; return codes, order and classification are unchanged
all 11 harness gates pass
scripts/gate_experiment.py plants one defect per gate in a clone and reports which gates catch it; a gate is only called possibly redundant when another gate that stays covers every case it catches
features.evidence: Full gate time fell from about 220 s to 75-85 s (tests gate 70 s); 93 test files, identical ordered output at 1 and 4 jobs, 12 jobs x5 stress, SIGINT/SIGTERM leave no process. process_adherence measured on 76 real sessions with no change to existing fields. feature_run_record.py: 30 tests, 3,324 budget cases with no loss and none left over budget. outside_agent.py: 131 tests. Reviews by a fresh subagent, codex-kiro and agy found about 30 defects across the rounds (lost features without an id, archive overwrite and path escape, kill diagnostics interleaving, --jobs swallowing a flag, orphaned queue after SIGTERM, credential-shaped guard names, unscrubbed error text); each got a failing test first. Not done: the 5-runs-per-version benchmark comparison, SubagentStop double counting is unverified, claude-kiro is not an independent reviewer for a Claude caller by design. Gate-necessity experiment (scripts/gate_experiment.py, 12 planted-defect cases, 32 tests): baseline passes; types, clean state, runtime drift and secret scan are each the only catch for their defect; registry, skill paths, bash compat, cred backends, hook wiring and state layer overlap with the tests gate but together cost about 2 s, so nothing is recommended for removal. A fresh subagent found three cases that could not trigger their gate, a missing baseline, and a clone of HEAD instead of the working tree; all fixed with tests.

features.name: AGY statusline: one adaptive line with model, context, quota
features.description: AGY's custom statusline shows only user@host:cwd and [ctx]. With stack_with_default true it is one row inside a block AGY owns, so it shifts when the native part changes height. Render one line from the AGY payload (model, effort, context percent and tokens, lowest 5h quota, git branch), dropping fields by priority to fit terminal_width, and stop stacking with the native line.
acceptance_criteria: the script prints exactly one line (no newline) that fits terminal_width at 60, 80 and 160 columns, dropping fields in a fixed priority order
AGY payload fields render: model.display_name, context_window.used_percentage with used/total tokens, and the lowest remaining 5h quota
Claude Code payloads, which lack quota and model.effort, still render cwd and context as before
the script still returns without waiting for EOF when stdin stays open
install_statusline writes and refreshes stack_with_default false for gemini
all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: scripts/tests/test_statusline_command.sh: 28 passed (failed first: 17 of 24 before the rewrite, 4 of 28 after the review). One adaptive line from the AGY payload (model, bar, used/total, lowest 5h quota, git branch), dropping bar, branch, quota, model, cwd, token detail to fit terminal_width; install_statusline and setup-host.sh write stack_with_default false. Live agy in a detached tmux pane after install.sh: 160 cols shows all fields, 70 cols drops bar and branch. A fresh subagent found 3 defects (zero-token fresh session dropped context and quota, CJK width counted in characters, trailing-slash or root cwd showed no directory); each got a failing test first. Live long-response probe (agy in tmux, 30 rows): the row went to the bottom once the pane filled and stayed there with the new script, the old script with stacking off, and the old script with stacking on, so the movement was not reproduced; in one longer run the row ended one line above the bottom after the response finished, not compared against the old script. One full-gate run reported 94 passed, 1 failed in the tests gate; the failing test name was lost because the output was cut with tail; a rerun of harness-verify.sh and five consecutive run-tests.sh --fast runs all passed 95/95, so the failure is unreproduced and unattributed. Not done: current_usage is null before the first turn and filled after it (input_tokens, output_tokens), so an out figure is available but not shown; the one-line-above-bottom end state is unexplained.
